title: SARS-CoV-2 Detection Using BGI RT-PCR Kit
author: Wei-Ting Lu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfc8jizw
materials: The QuantStudio software will open and the password for the locked template is covid192020 - this must be entered to allow for customisation of the eds file . Check the comments box under the properties tab for any comments made by the first reporter. The eds file automatically opens to the results page in log format. If the plate to be analysed is only half full, to remove any of the wells that are not to be analysed go to the plate screen and select these wells and deselect the targets.

Reagents are stored at -20ºC. Take out all the kit contents and thaw them thoroughly at ambient temperature. Vortex and centrifuge briefly. The enzyme mix should be kept on ice at all times. RT-PCR mastermix is aliquoted into PCR plates in designated hoods in the HTS tissue culture room. All personnel must have full PPE when entering the tissue culture room, which includes clean lab coat, fresh nitrile gloves, and full-face guard. Additionally, the individual pipetting in the hood must wear disposable forearm sleeves. Take required number of BGI RT-PCR kits from -20 °C freezer (2 Kits per 96w plate of RT-PCR reactions, 4 kits per full RNA plate since RT-PCR reactions are run in duplicates) and remove the 2019-nCoV Enzyme mix to maintain On ice , remove the Negative Control to -20 °C freezer, and allow the remaining tubes ( 2019-nCoV Reaction mix , Positive Control ) thaw up at Room temperature .

steps.title: Prepare PCR Master Mix Plates
steps.instruction: Dispense PCR Master mix into barcoded MicroAmp™ Fast optical 96-well plates.

substeps.instruction: Thaw 2019-nCoV Reaction mix and Enzyme mix tubes on ice; quick spin down all tubes.
For half plates: Use an electronic single channel pipette with filter tip to dispense 20µl of mix into individual wells.

For full plates: Transfer Master Mix into a 25ml reservoir using an L-1000 pipette with filtered tip. Dispense 20µl into all wells using an LTS 20-300µl multichannel pipette (Settings: Multi-Disp, Aliquot volume 20 µl, 8 aliquots, 1/1 Asp/Dsp Speed).
Eject remaining mix back into the reservoir.
Seal plates with AlumaSeal and verify seal integrity.
Transfer remaining Master Mix back into a Reaction Mix tube, label with date, and store in the fridge.

steps.title: Prepare Biomek Instrument
steps.instruction: Set up the Biomek FX instrument and deck for automated RNA transfer.

substeps.instruction: Clean the hood and all entering materials with DNA ZAP (Solution 1, then Solution 2, then wipe dry).
Wipe the deck with an RNaseZap wipe, followed by an alcohol wipe or 70% ethanol.
Purge Span-8 syringes until no bubbles are visible in tubing.
Check and refill Biomek FX Span-8 water container with Milli-Q water if necessary.
Place two boxes (lid off) of 50 μl filter tips on the deck.
Place a black microfuge tube rack in position P19.
Place an eppendorf tube (cap open) containing TET buffer in position A1 and the Positive Control tube (cap off) in position D1 of the microfuge rack.

steps.title: Load Samples and Reagents
steps.instruction: Load the RNA samples and qPCR reagent plates onto the Biomek deck.

substeps.instruction: Place the RNA sample plate (Eppendorf LoBind 96-well skirted plate) with the SPL barcode in position P16.
Pulse spin the ABI MicroAmp Optical plate (containing qPCR reagents mix) in a table top centrifuge if stored at 4 °C; stack it on a black Greiner CellStar plate and place in position P17.
Scan the barcodes of the qPCR plate and the RNA sample plate in Clarity LIMS to link them.

steps.title: Execute Automated Transfer
steps.instruction: Run the 'qPCR Setup' program within the 'Covid-19' project in the Biomek software.

substeps.instruction: Press the Run button (green triangle) to start the automated protocol:
1. Load 50mL tips (pod 1), aspirate 10mL RNA samples (10mL/sec), dispense 10mL to qPCR plate (10mL/sec), unload tips.
2. Load 50mL tip (pod 2), aspirate 10mL TET buffer from A1, dispense 10mL to qPCR plate G12 (negative control), unload tip.
3. Load 50mL tip (pod 2), aspirate 10mL Positive Control from D1 (20mL/sec), dispense 10mL to qPCR plate H12 (30mL/sec), unload tip.
Remove two tips from position G12 and H12 of the '50 μl Tips 1' box when prompted.
Remove the MicroAmp plate from the deck once the program is complete.
Seal the plate with MicroAmp Optical Adhesive Film and press down using the MicroAmp Adhesive Film Applicator.

steps.title: Post-Transfer Sample Management
steps.instruction: Secure the sample plates and prepare for PCR.

substeps.instruction: Seal the RNA sample plate using a Thermo Fisher PCR seal and store at -80 °C.
Home the instrument by selecting 'Home All Axes' under the Instrument menu.
Hand over the MicroAmp plates to the RT-PCR operator or store temporarily at 4 °C.

steps.title: PCR Plate Setup and Loading
steps.instruction: Prepare the PCR plate for the QuantStudio 3 machine.

substeps.instruction: Take the PCR plate to the PCR lab and scan the barcode into the 'plate handover' App in Chrome.
Check seal integrity and spin the plate briefly in an underbench centrifuge (1000 rpm, 1 minute).
Place the plate in the QuantStudio 3 sample drawer, ensuring the barcode is facing front and A1 is top-left.

steps.title: Configure PCR Run
steps.instruction: Set up the experiment parameters on the PCR machine laptop.

substeps.instruction: Open the 'design file' app in Chrome, scan the plate barcode, and hit SUBMIT.
Save the automatically downloaded text file to the 'Plate Layout' folder on the Desktop using the barcode as the filename.
Open 'Covid-19 Mater Template.edt' from the Desktop.
Scan the plate barcode into the Barcode and Name fields; enter the Crick user name in the User field.
Import the plate setup by browsing to the text file in 'Desktop\Plate Layout' and clicking 'Apply' (confirm 'yes' to replace info).
Under 'Method', enter password 'covid192020'.
Under 'Plate' (Advanced Setup Tab), set Target1: FAM, Quencher: None (Covid-19) and Target2: VIC, Quencher: None (Internal Control).
Under 'Plate' (Quick Setup Tab), set Passive Reference Dye: None.

steps.title: Run and Export PCR Data
steps.instruction: Execute the PCR run and export the resulting data files.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Start Run' in the Run window.
Save the barcode.eds file in the 'Covid19 Results' folder on the Desktop.
Verify the run duration is 01:28:41.
Export the EDS file to the 'Primary Review' shared drive using the unique patient barcode as the filename.

steps.title: Primary Data Review
steps.instruction: Perform the first check of the PCR results in Quantstudio 1.4.

substeps.instruction: Set threshold to automatic and check the amplification plot for whole-plate failure.

Verify controls: Negative controls (TET Buffer/extraction control) must have Ct > 37 (FAM) and > 35 (VIC/HEX) or be undetermined. Positive controls must show exponential amplification with Ct ≤ 37 (FAM) and ≤ 35 (VIC/HEX).
Enter the reporter's name in the properties tab 'user' box.
Review all samples; right-click and select 'OMIT' for samples to be excluded.
Save the checked .eds file to the /report1 folder.
Extract plate genealogy data from ClarityLims to document the history of the plate.

steps.title: Secondary Validation and Final Analysis
steps.instruction: A second reporter validates the results via the online portal.

substeps.instruction: Download the run results and duplicates via the web app.
Repeat the control checks (Positive: FAM ≤ 37, VIC/HEX ≤ 35; Negative: FAM > 37, VIC/HEX > 35 or no data).
Verify the overall plate curves and audit trail.
Adjust baseline manually (between 3 to 15 cycles) if necessary by unticking 'auto baseline' in the linear graph.
Adjust threshold manually if necessary by unticking 'auto threshold' in the log scale graph to remove noise.
Mark samples as 'INVALID' if they show non-exponential amplification with Ct < 37 (covid) and < 35 (internal).
Fail the plate if negative controls show signal < 35 (IC) or < 37 (covid), or if positive controls show no signal for either target.

steps.title: Final Result Export
steps.instruction: Export and upload the final validated data to the LIMS.

substeps.instruction: Export the analyzed results from QuantStudio as a .xls file (not .xlsx).
Upload both the .xls file and the modified .eds file to the online portal and click 'Validate'.
Drop the final result files to the sFTP server RESULTS folder with unique names.
